Growth assessment 2026-Q2 · Eurostat quarterly national accounts
Executive assessmentReal GDP grew 4.6% year-on-year in 2026-Q2 and the growth mix is classified as external-sector-led growth. The largest positive engine was net exports, while the contribution mix is assessed as mixed. Domestic demand contributed +2.2 pp and net exports +3.0 pp. The decomposition covers 100% of the six core expenditure components. The component sum differs from headline GDP growth by -0.6 pp, so the decomposition should be read with caution. Watchpoints: Contribution reconciliation gap -0.56 pp; Investment supporting growth; External sector supporting growth; Strong household-demand contribution.

Executive structural synthesis

Denmark's quarterly national-accounts picture is classified as broadly constructive structural picture. Growth Quality: External-sector-led growth. Investment Quality: Productive-capital intensive. Competitiveness: Broad competitiveness improvement. Household Demand: Durable-led discretionary demand. External Sector: Export-supported external contribution. Across the five modules, 3 are favourable, 2 mixed/neutral and 0 adverse.

Investment structure & quality

The fixed-investment mix in 2026-Q2 is classified as productive-capital intensive. GFCF stood at 22.1% of GDP versus 21.5% for EU-27. Machinery/equipment plus intellectual property accounted for 54.9% of GFCF, while construction accounted for 45.2%. Total real GFCF growth was +3.1% year-on-year in 2026-Q2. Watchpoints: High intellectual-property share.

Productivity, labour cost & competitiveness

The current structural signal is classified as broad competitiveness improvement. On the latest common comparison quarter (2026-Q2), real labour productivity per hour grew +3.5% year-on-year versus +0.8% in EU-27. Nominal unit labour cost per hour increased -1.3% versus +2.8% in EU-27. Watchpoints: Large productivity gap versus EU; Large NULC gap versus EU.

Household demand & consumption mix

The current household-demand mix is classified as durable-led discretionary demand. Real household consumption grew +1.8% year-on-year in 2026-Q2. Durables accounted for 10.7% of nominal household expenditure and services for 58.1% in 2026-Q2.

External sector & trade contribution

The external-sector contribution is classified as export-supported external contribution. Net exports contributed +3.00 percentage points to GDP growth in 2026-Q2. Methodology and interpretation

The growth-regime, growth-balance and watchpoint labels are transparent A-CLUSTER analytical rules. They are not Eurostat classifications. The report chooses the latest quarter with headline real GDP growth and a sufficiently populated expenditure decomposition. Structural indicators such as productivity, unit labour costs and GFCF may have different release lags; their observation quarter is disclosed explicitly. The household durability module (namq_10_fcs) follows the domestic consumption concept and is not identical to the household/NPISH aggregate used in the GDP expenditure decomposition. A reconciliation residual larger than ±0.35 percentage points is flagged rather than silently treated as a complete decomposition.
Data source: Eurostat datasets namq_10_gdp, namq_10_lp_ulc, namq_10_an6 and namq_10_fcs.
